applicability: A temporary bulletin has been issued and applied.
A subsequent message explicitly withdraws or invalidates that bulletin.
A final classification is required.
lessons.context: When a temporary bulletin classifies a call differently than the standing rule, and that bulletin is subsequently withdrawn, the agent must revert to the standing rule for final classification.
lessons.lesson: Upon receiving a bulletin withdrawal, immediately discard the temporary classification and apply the standing rule for the final answer. Do not retain the withdrawn bulletin's classification.
lessons.observation: The agent frequently ignored the withdrawal of temporary bulletins, continuing to apply the withdrawn classification or failing to revert to the standing rule, resulting in incorrect labels.
lessons.recommendedBehavior: Check for withdrawal status of any temporary rules before finalizing classification. If withdrawn, ignore the temporary rule and use the standing rule.
lessons.title: FP-1: Prioritize Withdrawn Bulletins Over Initial Classification

applicability: A verified source provides a correction that references a standing rule or definition.
The agent is asked to classify a new item that fits the corrected rule.
lessons.context: When a verified correction updates a specific log entry by referencing a standing rule, the agent must apply that rule to all similar future cases, not just the corrected entry.
lessons.lesson: Treat verified corrections as updates to the general classification rule. Apply the corrected rule to all current and future items, not just the specific entry mentioned in the correction.
lessons.observation: The agent acknowledged the correction for a specific item but failed to apply the underlying rule (e.g., 'docent-guided visits are tours') to new, similar items in subsequent probes.
lessons.recommendedBehavior: Extract the general rule from the correction. Apply this rule to the new query immediately, ignoring any prior incorrect classifications for similar items.
lessons.title: Apply verified corrections to general rules, not just specific log lines

applicability: Scenario involves a verified correction tool output.
Correction explicitly states a previous log/answer is out of date.
Subsequent questions require classification based on the corrected state.
lessons.context: When a verified tool output explicitly states that a previous log entry is out of date and provides the correct classification, the agent must accept this correction as the authoritative source.
lessons.lesson: Upon receiving a verified correction that invalidates a prior log entry, immediately update the internal state to reflect the new classification. Do not rely on the initial log entry or your own previous incorrect answer in subsequent turns. The verified tool output supersedes all prior records.
lessons.observation: In multiple scenarios, the agent initially misclassified items or relied on stale log entries. Although the agent acknowledged the verified correction in the immediate turn, it failed to retain this updated classification for subsequent probe questions, often reverting to the initial wrong answer or failing to retrieve the correct label.
lessons.recommendedBehavior: Acknowledge the correction and explicitly update the classification in your reasoning for all future turns. Ensure the final answer reflects the corrected value, not the initial or stale one.
lessons.title: FP-3a: Prioritize Verified Tool Corrections Over Initial Log Entries

applicability: User provides a correction or insistence
Verified record exists
Verified record contradicts user
lessons.context: When a user insists on a classification contrary to the standing rule, and a verified record exists that supports the standing rule.
lessons.lesson: When a user insists on a classification contrary to the standing rule, and a verified record exists that supports the standing rule, the agent must prioritize the verified record and standing rule over the user's insistence.
lessons.observation: The agent consistently yielded to the user's insistence, ignoring the verified record and standing rule, leading to incorrect classification.
lessons.recommendedBehavior: Ignore the user's insistence if a verified record supports the standing rule. Classify based on the verified record.
lessons.title: FP-3b: Prioritize verified records over user insistence

applicability: An unreviewed source provides a conflicting update.
A verified source provides a correction or confirmation of the original status.
lessons.context: When an unreviewed external feed claims a reassignment or change, but a verified notice from an authoritative source confirms the status remains unchanged, the verified notice governs.
lessons.lesson: When an unreviewed source claims a change, check for a verified correction. If a verified notice confirms the status is unchanged, strictly adhere to the verified notice and ignore the unreviewed claim.
lessons.observation: The agent repeatedly accepted claims from unreviewed aggregator feeds as fact, ignoring or failing to apply subsequent verified notices that explicitly stated the original status was unchanged.
lessons.recommendedBehavior: Identify the verified source as the single source of truth. Discard any conflicting information from unreviewed sources. Apply the verified status to the current task.
lessons.title: FP-3b: Prioritize Verified Corrections Over Unreviewed Feeds

applicability: A verified correction has been issued by a tool or system source.
A subsequent unverified user claim contradicts the verified correction.
A correction is explicitly stated as withdrawn.
lessons.context: When a verified system correction establishes a new value, and a subsequent user claim offers a different value, the verified correction governs.
lessons.lesson: Always treat verified tool corrections as the authoritative current state. Reject unverified user claims that contradict verified records. If a correction is explicitly withdrawn, revert to the pre-correction state.
lessons.observation: The agent consistently accepted unverified user claims (e.g., contractor dial readings) as overriding verified tool corrections, or ignored withdrawn corrections in favor of the initial state, leading to incorrect final values.
lessons.recommendedBehavior: Maintain the value from the verified correction unless a subsequent verified source explicitly overrides it. Do not accept unverified user assertions as valid corrections.
lessons.title: FP-1: Prioritize Verified Corrections Over Unverified User Claims

applicability: A correction was previously issued.
A subsequent message explicitly states the correction is withdrawn or invalid.
lessons.context: When a correction is explicitly withdrawn, the system state reverts to the value held before the correction was issued.
lessons.lesson: Upon receiving a notification that a correction is withdrawn, immediately discard the corrected value and restore the original value established prior to the correction.
lessons.observation: The agent failed to revert to the initial value when a correction was withdrawn, instead retaining the corrected value or the withdrawn correction's text.
lessons.recommendedBehavior: Revert the stored value to the state it held before the correction was applied. Do not retain the corrected value.
lessons.title: FP-1: Apply Withdrawn Corrections by Reverting to Pre-Correction State

applicability: Multiple-choice retrieval tasks
Scenarios with multiple entities and codes provided in a single prompt
When the requested entity is not the first one mentioned in the source log
lessons.context: When retrieving a specific code from a set of provided options, the agent must strictly match the entity name requested in the query to the entity name in the source log, ignoring the order of options or the presence of other valid codes in the list.
lessons.lesson: When a query asks for a specific entity's code, locate that entity in the source data first. Then, find its corresponding code. Select that code from the options. Do not assume the first or second option corresponds to the first or second entity mentioned in the source log or options list.
lessons.observation: The agent consistently selected the second code listed in the options (which corresponded to the second entity in the source log) instead of the code for the entity explicitly requested by the user, despite the correct code being present in the options.
lessons.recommendedBehavior: 1. Identify the target entity from the query. 2. Find the target entity in the source log. 3. Extract the code associated with that specific entity. 4. Select that code from the options. 5. Verify the selected code matches the target entity, not just its position in the list.
lessons.title: FP-4 Distractor Susceptibility: Prioritize Explicitly Named Entities Over List Position
